mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to recover from its recent trough, weekday trip chaining should increase and pull RETAIL_REC modestly upward over the next four weeks as commuters add discretionary stops after work.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 4 weeks even though WORKPLACES keeps improving for two more consecutive weeks and TRANSIT does not fall further.

mechanism_narrative: A continuing shift toward RESIDENTIAL time suppresses outside shopping visits, so RETAIL_REC should fall over the next two weeks when RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above baseline.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays at or above +8 points for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining at or above +8 and no simultaneous rebound in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve together, the shared return of commuting and downtown activity should raise RETAIL_REC within four weeks by increasing exposure to retail corridors.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are higher than their prior-week levels for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM above its recent range indicates fewer substitution trips to essential retail, which should free demand for discretionary shopping and lift RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above +7 points and stays there for one weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week after GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +7, or it falls while GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A deeper decline in PARKS use alongside weaker TRANSIT signals a broad loss of outdoor and downtown movement that will also drag RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while PARKS and TRANSIT both remain below their current week levels.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES drops further below its recent level, consumers will concentrate trips closer to home and RETAIL_REC will weaken over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after WORKPLACES falls by more than 3 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, renewed weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES should precede lower retail visitation, so RETAIL_REC will fall over the next four weeks if both mobility channels keep deteriorating.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite continuing declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES and no drop in RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in GROCERY_PHARM together with a partial rebound in PARKS signals broader activity normalization, which should turn RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +5 while PARKS improves by at least 3 points from its recent weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not outperform its prior 28-day average over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM stays above +5 and PARKS improves by at least 3 points.
